approach: Move the job's Score out of the close-time landing commit and commit it from the landing queue, as a records-only commit made right after that job's host landing, under the drain's landing lock. The Score is the one closing record the queue can rebuild from records already at head. `expected_score` recomputes it, so no spool is needed. The other closing records are held in memory in `Closing` until close. Three of them (candidate, verification, Outcome Landed) are read by `land_pr` and `landed_commit_from_records` at or before the landing commit. That is out of scope (gh/landing.rs). Invocations feed reconcile and the Score. The doc states this narrower scope as a fixed limit. It is raised below as the first open question, which the user must accept. The caller chooses deferral: a new `Athena::go_for_queue` sets a `defer_score` flag, and only the real drain at max_in_flight > 1 uses it. `go`, `go_with_stages` and max_in_flight = 1 are unchanged. `RealSteps::land` calls the new `Athena::commit_landed_records` in the `Landing::Landed` arm only. `athena land` calls it after a Landed report so a deferred job landed outside the drain still gets its Score. Append-only is enforced by the gate's existing `Rule::AppendOnly` in every Athena commit. The commits.rs change adds only the skip of identical bytes and the no-empty-commit rule. Criterion 3 is shown through the production commit path (`Committer::commit_records`) and by the check that every queue records commit shows only 'A' lines.

decisions.choice: Defer only the Score, and state the reason correctly. The Score can be rebuilt after landing from records already at head (athena_gate::jobs::expected_score loads the job's invocations, candidate, verification and outcome from the tree). Nothing has to be stored between close and landing. Its value does not depend on the head; with `at` = the close time it is the same value as at close. The move is chosen for ordering and storage, not value: the Score is the only closing record that is derived and so needs no spool. The doc says exactly this.
decisions.reason: Invocations, plans, critiques and baseline live only in memory in `Closing` (close.rs push_closing_records), so deferring them would need a per-job spool in the state directory, and invocations feed reconcile (Rule::Reconciliation). Candidate, verification and Outcome Landed are read by `land_pr` at head, and `landed_commit_from_records` finds the landing commit as the one that introduced outcome-landed.json (landing.rs 55-75, 708-718). None of that can move while gh/landing.rs is out of scope. The gate has no rule that requires the Score in the same commit as Outcome Landed (jobs.rs check judges only scores a commit adds, against expected_score of that commit's tree).

rejected.why: Breaks `land_pr` (verification and candidate read at head) and the landed-commit lookup (outcome-landed.json). It needs gh/landing.rs changes, which are out of scope, and a spool for the in-memory records.

rejected.option: Defer invocations, plans, critiques, baseline and Score through a state-directory spool
rejected.why: New persistence and crash recovery (recovery is out of scope), and invocations feed reconcile that `land_pr` runs first. The gain over Score-only is not shown, and the risk is high for one producer run.

rejected.why: Hook only; the brief forbids a default no-op as the only implementation.

decisions.choice: The caller chooses deferral. `Athena::go_for_queue` sets `defer_score`, carried through `Outputs` and `RunContext` in run/mod.rs and read in `land_or_block`. Only `RealSteps::run` passes it, and only when `[drain.pipeline] max_in_flight` > 1. `go` and `go_with_stages` pass false.
decisions.reason: A config switch inside close.rs would leave jobs closed by plain `athena go` and landed by `athena land` with no Score. The threading must go through run/mod.rs because `Outputs`, `RunContext` and the `go*` entry points are defined only there (lines ~267-330, 964-987). Findings 1 and 2 (run/mod.rs and main.rs are outside the deliverables) are answered: both files stay in the plan, each with one small, stated change, and open question 2 asks the user to accept them. No smaller file set works, as the rejected options show.

decisions.choice: Where the Score commit is published (finding 3): it is a records-only commit on the local branch directly after its job's landing commit. This change does not push it. It travels the way `plan_rebase` (landing.rs 573-591) already carries records-only commits that follow a landing commit on the first-parent chain: it is rebased onto the host's main with the next landing's `rebase_job_branch`. The last Score of a drain therefore stays local until the next landing or a sync. The doc states this. The criterion 1 test asserts what can be checked locally: each Score commit is a descendant of its own landing commit on the first-parent chain, and it adds only its own job's Score. Pushing it needs landing.rs, so it is a stated limit and open question 3, not a silent local-only commit.
decisions.reason: Both the local landing commit and any later records-only commit already live only on the local branch until a landing carries them. The plan reads that as the existing publication path and adds no push in a file that is out of scope. I read `plan_rebase` and `land_pr`; I did not run a rebase over a Score commit, so whether it carries cleanly is checked by the producer's spike (step 1).

rejected.option: Push the Score commit from RealSteps::land
rejected.why: `land_pr` and `check_push` own pushes and allow only the work branch; a new push path is landing.rs territory.

rejected.option: Write the Score to the athena/records branch through the landing-records sink
rejected.why: The sink is built inside `land_pr` (landing.rs 745-772) and is out of scope.

decisions.choice: `commit_landed_records(job, ui)` recomputes the Score with `expected_score` at head, using the closing Outcome's `at` and `RulesVersion::CURRENT`. It returns None when the job has no Outcome Landed at head or already has a Score. The call site is the guard against committing before the host landing (finding 6): Outcome Landed is written at close, so the function cannot tell a host-landed job from a locally closed one. Its doc comment says so, and the criterion 2 test pins that a NotLanded job gets no Score commit.
decisions.reason: The gate accepts a Score equal to `expected_score` for its own `at`. The close time keeps an intervention made between close and landing out of the closing Score. No channel between `go` and the drain is needed, and the call is idempotent. I did not find a cheap host-state check in core that does not read the link state in landing.rs.

rejected.why: Folds an intervention made between close and landing into the closing Score instead of leaving it for a re-score.

rejected.option: Carry the close-time Score from go to the drain
Check the pull request link state inside commit_landed_records

decisions.choice: Append-only (finding 5): the enforcement is the gate's existing `Rule::AppendOnly`, run by `build_commit_in` for every Athena commit. Add one helper, `Committer::commit_new_records`, that drops files whose bytes at head are identical (they would be empty or no-op commits) and returns head with no commit when none remain; it passes every other file to the normal gated commit, so a same-path different-bytes write is refused by the gate. The doc states the confirmed reading: record paths are unique per record (records/<kind>/<month>/<id>.json and records/jobs/<id>/...), so two jobs in one month shard add different files and never conflict, and a same-path conflict is refused, never merged or rewritten. Criterion 3 is shown through the production path, `Committer::commit_records`.
decisions.reason: The rule already exists and is tested (content.rs); a second check would duplicate it. The identical-bytes skip is the only thing the queue needs that the gate does not give, because a retried or repeated call must not fail or make an empty commit.

rejected.option: A second refusal check of the helper's own, with the conflict planted by raw plumbing
rejected.why: Duplicates Rule::AppendOnly. The in-process gate would refuse first, so the extra check could not be reached.

rejected.option: Resolve a same-path conflict by keeping both sides
rejected.why: The queue's commits are plumbing commits on head under the repository lock and never rebase. Distinct paths do not conflict; a same-path conflict is refused.

risks.risk: A deferred job whose landing is NotLanded or Waiting has no Score until it lands.

risks.risk: After the host merge the local branch moves, so the Score commit builds on a moved head.

risks.risk: Tests with concurrent jobs are flaky.
risks.mitigation: No sleeps. Order comes from the lander double's call order and at-call-time assertions, with channels only where an order must be forced.

demonstrations.method: New test in tests/drain.rs with `Fixture::with_config(&pipelined(3))`. Three steward requests are drained by `drain_concurrent(&steps, work_everything(), &Quiet, 3)`. `steps` is `RealSteps` over an Athena from `fx.athena(scenario)`, so the real go, close, gate and commit code runs. The lander double records its call order and, at each call, loads Records at head and asserts this job has no Score yet and every job landed earlier has one. After the drain it lists the Score commits with `git log --reverse` and builds one aligned table: landing position, job, Score commit and its position. It asserts the Score commits are in landing order and that each is a descendant of its own landing commit on the first-parent chain.
demonstrations.observes: The Score commits appear in git log in the lander's recorded landing order. At each lander call the job being landed has no Score and its predecessors have one, so none is committed before its landing. A failure prints the landing sequence beside the Score commit sequence for the three jobs. The test also records that the Score commits are local and are not pushed (finding 3).
demonstrations.fails_without: If the Score were still committed at close, every job's Score would exist before its landing and the at-call-time assertion would fail. If `RealSteps::land` did not commit, the Score commits would be missing and the log check would fail. If commits were out of landing order, the order check would fail.
